# Motivation & Problem Statement

## Why Quality Control Needs AI

---

<!-- _class: dense -->

![bg left:38%](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1581091226825-a6a2a5aee158?w=1200&auto=format&fit=crop)

# Industry 4.0 & Quality Control

Modern manufacturing produces **millions of parts per day** — far too fast for human inspection alone.

- 🏭 Global defect-related losses: **$300 B+/year**
- 👁️ Human inspectors: effective but **inconsistent after 20 minutes**
- ⚙️ Traditional rule-based systems **fail on novel defect types**
- 📊 Machine vision has 97 % precision — but **only on seen defect patterns**

<div class="callout">

### Key Insight
Defect types evolve with new materials and processes. Systems must **learn continuously**, not just classify.

</div>

---

# Problem Statement

<div class="cols">
<div class="col">

### Given
- High-speed production line with camera sensors
- Heterogeneous product variants
- Rare, imbalanced defect classes
- Real-time constraint: < 50 ms per part

</div>
<div class="col">

### Goal
Design an ML system that:
1. Detects defects with ≥ 98 % recall
2. Generalises to **unseen defect types**
3. Operates **on-device** (edge hardware)
4. Requires **minimal labelled data**

</div>
</div>

<div class="callout warning">

### Challenge
Only **0.3 %** of produced parts are defective → extreme class imbalance must be handled explicitly.

</div>

---

# Background &
# Related Work

## Foundations in Computer Vision & Anomaly Detection

---

<!-- _class: dense -->

![bg right:35%](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1620712943543-bcc4688e7485?w=1200&auto=format&fit=crop)

# Relevant Prior Work

| Approach | Strength | Limitation |
|:---------|:---------|:-----------|
| Classical CV (thresholding) | Fast, interpretable | Brittle, manual tuning |
| CNN classifiers | High accuracy on known classes | Needs large labelled dataset |
| Autoencoders (AE) | Unsupervised, detects novelty | Blurry reconstructions |
| GAN-based anomaly | Strong generative model | Training instability |
| **Ours: Patch-SVDD + SSL** | Few-shot, generalises | — |

<div class="callout">

### Research Gap
No existing method combines **few-shot generalisation** with **on-edge real-time inference** for multi-variant manufacturing.

</div>

---

# Theoretical Background

<div class="cols">
<div class="col">

## Self-Supervised Learning

Pre-train on **unlabelled** normal images using:
- Rotation prediction
- Jigsaw puzzle solving
- Contrastive loss (SimCLR)

Builds rich visual representations **without labels**.

</div>
<div class="col">

## SVDD (Support Vector Data Description)

Learns a **minimum-volume hypersphere** around normal feature vectors.

At inference:
- Distance from centre → anomaly score
- Threshold → binary decision

Scales well to edge hardware.

</div>
</div>

---

# Proposed Approach

## Patch-SVDD with Self-Supervised Pre-Training

---

# System Architecture

![bg right:44%](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614680376593-902f74cf0d41?w=1200&auto=format&fit=crop)

**Three-stage pipeline:**

**① Pre-training**
SSL on 50 k unlabelled normal images → feature extractor backbone

**② Few-shot Adaptation**
SVDD fitted on **50–200 normal samples** per product variant → no defect labels needed

**③ Real-time Inference**
Patch-level anomaly map → part-level decision in **< 40 ms** on edge GPU

---

# Data Pipeline

<div class="cols">
<div class="col">

### Input
- 2 × 4 K line-scan cameras
- 120 parts / minute throughput
- 7 product families, 43 variants

### Augmentation
- Random crop + resize
- Colour jitter (±15 %)
- Simulated lighting variation

</div>
<div class="col">

### Pre-processing
```python
transform = Compose([
    RandomResizedCrop(224),
    RandomHorizontalFlip(),
    ColorJitter(0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
    ToTensor(),
    Normalize(μ, σ),
])
```

### Output
Feature map: **512-d vector** per 32 × 32 patch

</div>
</div>

---

# Training Strategy

<style scoped>section { font-size: 17pt; }</style>

| Phase | Data | Epochs | Loss |
|:------|:-----|-------:|:-----|
| SSL pre-training | 50 k unlabelled normals | 200 | SimCLR NT-Xent |
| SVDD fine-tuning | 50–200 normal per variant | 50 | Hypersphere loss |
| Threshold calibration | 500 normal + 100 defective | — | F1 maximisation |

# Experimental Results

## Benchmarks, Ablation & Comparison

---

# Experimental Setup

<div class="cols">
<div class="col">

### Dataset: MVTec-AD + IndustrialNet
- **15 000** test images, 15 object categories
- Defect types: scratches, holes, contamination, colour deviation
- Held-out: 3 product families **never seen during pre-training**

### Hardware
- Training: 2 × NVIDIA A100 (80 GB)
- Inference: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32 GB

</div>
<div class="col">

### Baselines
| Model | Params | Labels needed |
|:------|-------:|:-------------|
| ResNet-50 + FC | 25 M | Thousands |
| PatchCore | 12 M | None |
| **Ours (Patch-SVDD)** | **3.2 M** | **None** |

### Metrics
- **AUROC** (primary)
- **F1 @ 98 % Recall** (operational)
- **FPS** on edge device

</div>
</div>

---

# Results — AUROC by Category

<style scoped>section { font-size: 16pt; }</style>

<div class="result-bar"><div class="result-bar-label">Texture defects</div><div class="result-bar-track"><div class="result-bar-fill" style="width:97%">97.1 %</div></div></div>

<div class="callout" style="margin-top:18px">

**Mean AUROC: 95.5 %** — outperforms PatchCore (93.8 %) and ResNet-50 baseline (89.2 %) while using **7× fewer parameters**.

</div>

---

![bg right:40%](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551288049-bebda4e38f71?w=1200&auto=format&fit=crop)

# Ablation Study

Which components matter most?

| Configuration | AUROC |
|:--------------|------:|
| Full model | **95.5 %** |
| w/o SSL pre-training | 87.3 % |
| w/o patch-level SVDD | 91.0 % |
| w/o data augmentation | 93.1 % |
| ResNet backbone only | 89.2 % |

→ SSL pre-training contributes **+8.2 pp** — the single biggest factor.

---

# Conclusion &
# Future Work

---

# Contributions & Conclusions

<div class="cols">
<div class="col">

### What was done
1. Combined **SSL pre-training + SVDD** for unsupervised anomaly detection
2. Validated on real production-line data across **43 product variants**
3. Achieved **38 ms inference** on edge hardware without accuracy loss
4. Demonstrated **zero-shot generalisation** to unseen product families (91.7 % AUROC)

</div>
<div class="col">

### Key Takeaways
- Self-supervised pre-training is **far more sample-efficient** than supervised approaches
- Patch-level scoring enables **localisation** without segmentation labels
- System is ready for **pilot deployment** at partner company

</div>
</div>

---

![bg right:35%](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1684369175833-4b445ad6bfb5?w=1200&auto=format&fit=crop)

# Future Work

<div class="callout">

### Short Term (6 months)
**Continual learning** — adapt SVDD online as new defect types emerge in production without catastrophic forgetting

</div>

<div class="callout">

### Medium Term (12 months)
**Multi-sensor fusion** — combine RGB, depth, and vibration signals for richer anomaly signals on metal castings

</div>

<div class="callout warning">

### Open Question
Can we build a **single foundation model** fine-tunable to any production line with < 10 minutes of data collection?

</div>
